rektion: die Sonne scheint (auf + Akk.); jd. scheint + Adj. / zu + Inf. (er scheint müde zu sein)
meaning_en: to shine; to seem, to appear
definition_de: 1. Licht ausstrahlen (die Sonne, der Mond scheint); 2. den Eindruck machen, wirken (sie scheint glücklich zu sein, es scheint, dass ...)
example_de: Nach tagelangem Regen scheint endlich wieder die Sonne, und die Leute im Biergarten scheinen glücklich.
example_en: After days of rain the sun is finally shining again, and the people in the beer garden seem happy.
visual_idea: Collocation 'die Sonne scheint' + 'glücklich scheinen': one sunny scene carries both everyday meanings. Sunbeams breaking through the last clouds over a wet beer garden show 'shine'; people with closed eyes and smiling faces turned to the sun show 'seem happy'. Beat a tired commuter yawning in the S-Bahn ('er scheint müde zu sein' reads as gähnen) and a full moon over a lake (only the literal meaning, less everyday).
